newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives vote again for leader on June 17.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives vote again for leader on June 17.

text.p: Conservative MPs will vote again to choose their leader on June 17 after none of the five current candidates won enough support to take the first round outright.

Former Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke won 49 votes, short of the level needed to win outright, followed by four other former ministers: William Hague with 41, John Redwood with 27, Peter Lilley with 24 and Michael Howard with 23.

Nominations for the June 17 ballot close at 1100 GMT on Thursday, June 12. Most observers expect at least one of the candidates in Tuesday's ballot to step down. But to complicate matters, the rules say new candidates can enter the race.

The rules for the second ballot are eased to make a victor more likely. In the first round Clarke would have needed the votes of more than half of all 164 Conservative MPs and a margin of 15 percent over his nearest challenger for outright victory.
To win on the second ballot, a simple majority (83 votes) is needed. If there is no winner on June 17, the two front-runners will square off in a third and final ballot on June 19.
